subject: POC capacity planning for Acme AI - proposal and next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acme.ai>, Olivia Park <olivia.park@acme.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-10T15:23:00-07:00
Subject: Recap + info we need for POC capacity planning

Thanks again for the demo today - great conversation. Per our discussion, I've put together a short list of items we need to finalize the POC capacity plan so we can scope reserved GPUs, autoscaling behavior, and burst expectations. Can you please confirm the items below and fill in any gaps?

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- Goal: Evaluate 1-shot and multi-turn chat flows for Acme Search Assistant using the open Llama-2-70B variant you mentioned.
- Success criteria: 95th %ile response latency < 300ms for short queries, relevance score > 0.8 on your internal eval set, and ability to sustain peak business-hour load without timeouts.

Info requested from Acme to finalize plan:
1) Expected concurrent users / QPS during peak (business hours).
2) Typical prompt and context sizes (average tokens and max tokens).
3) Length of the POC (target start date and duration).
4) Expected burst characteristics (how often and how large are bursts).
5) Any hard budget or cost targets we should design around.

Next steps from Redwood:
- We'll propose a capacity profile (reserved GPUs + autoscale limits) and an evaluation timeline.
- Dylan will provide engineering notes on model quantization and memory tradeoffs.
- We'll share a draft capacity plan and a short runbook for the POC.

Attachments: example prompts CSV and a baseline capacity plan draft (I'll circulate a formal PDF after we get your numbers).

Thanks - aiming to get the capacity proposal to you by Friday if we have the numbers.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Olivia Park <olivia.park@acme.ai>
Date: 2026-05-11T09:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap + info we need for POC capacity planning

Thanks Marissa - quick answers below. Appreciate the clear checklist.

1) Peak concurrency: ~120 concurrent active users for the search assistant during peak. That translates roughly to 60-80 QPS for short queries; occasional spikes up to ~160 QPS during large marketing pushes.
2) Prompt sizes: typical query ~30 tokens. With system + conversation context avg ~550 tokens, max around 1,800 tokens for long support sessions. Generations average ~60 tokens.
3) POC duration: Prefer a 4-week evaluation starting the week of June 1. We can be flexible by a week.
4) Burst expectations: Marketing-led bursts happen 2-3x per week and last ~15-20 minutes; during those bursts, QPS can 2x-3x baseline for short periods.
5) Budget: We'd like to keep incremental infra spend under $10k for the POC if possible; total cost isn't a hard blocker but helpful to know for procurement.

Let us know what you recommend for reserved vs autoscale capacity. Happy to jump on a short follow-up with Dev and Dylan.

- Samir
Head of Product, Acme AI
samir.khan@acme.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acme.ai>, Olivia Park <olivia.park@acme.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-12T11:36:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed capacity profile + timeline (draft)

Samir - thanks for the details. Based on your numbers above we've put together a draft POC capacity profile. High-level proposal:

POC timeline:
- Start: Week of June 1, 2026 (toggleable by one week)
- Duration: 4 weeks active evaluation

Reserved capacity (to ensure baseline SLOs):
- Reserved: 2x A100-80GB instances (shared across sessions) with Redwood Dedicated allocation - provides predictable baseline throughput to keep 95th %ile latency in target during normal business hours.

Autoscaling + burst profile:
- Autoscale floor: reserved capacity (2 GPUs)
- Autoscale max: 8 GPUs during sustained higher load (up to ~24 hours)
- Burst / emergency cap: temporary burst to 12 GPUs for short spikes (15-30 minutes) - throttled by policy and cost guardrails.

Estimated throughput/latency: with quantized Llama-2-70B and batching optimizations we expect to be able to handle ~70-100 QPS on 2 GPUs for short queries with 95th %ile latency target ~250-350ms depending on batching and avg token length. With autoscale to 8 GPUs we can cover your 160 QPS spikes with headroom.

Cost note: rough incremental infra estimate for the 4-week window with the above profile is $8k- $12k depending on actual burst usage. We'll work with finance/ops to keep you under the $10k target where feasible.

Ownership and ops:
- Redwood ops lead for the POC: Dylan Brooks (dylan.brooks@redwood.ai) - will own provision, monitoring hooks, and runbook for fallbacks.
- Sales/contract owner: Marissa Cole.

Action items:
- Samir/Olivia: confirm start week and whether procurement needs an SOW for reserved capacity.
- Acme procurement: if SOW needed, please share contract/contact.
- Redwood: we'll circulate a formal capacity plan PDF and a short evaluation runbook (includes test prompts and monitoring dashboards).

Attaching the draft capacity plan and example prompts for your internal eval.

Thanks - happy to jump on a 20-min sync if it helps.

Best,
Marissa
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acme.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-13T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Proposed capacity profile + timeline (draft)

Quick technical notes to complement Marissa's draft:
- Model / memory: Llama-2-70B will fit comfortably on A100-80GB with int8 quantization; recommended to test FP16 vs int8 for quality tradeoffs.
- KV cache: given the 1,800 token max context, we recommend session affinity to avoid cold KV-cache penalties for long sessions. That increases GPU memory usage per session; plan reserves account for that.
- Batching: we'll enable adaptive batching for short queries to improve throughput; batching will slightly increase median latency but helps reduce unit cost. We'll expose batching windows in the runbook so you can adjust quality vs cost.
- Monitoring: we'll wire up per-route 95/99 latency, token/prompt counts, and cost-by-token dashboards. Alerts for sustained autoscale > 75% of max for > 30m.

I'll join any technical sync and can provide more specific perf numbers with a short synthetic run later this week if you want.

- Dylan
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@acme.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-14T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Proposed capacity profile + timeline (draft)

One more data point from engineering:
- For the Llama-2-70B quantized path we're assuming average generation tokens of 60 and avg context of 550 tokens which maps to ~1.3GB GEMM working set per request on int8. If your real-world prompts skew much larger we'll need to increase reserved capacity or lean on higher autoscale headroom.
- If you'd like to reduce baseline reserved costs we can run the POC with 1 reserved GPU + 4 max autoscale and add a short warm-up phase to prepopulate caches; tradeoff is slightly higher tail latency for new sessions.

Happy to do a short load test with your sample prompts (you can drop them in the Drive link).

- Dev
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Proposed capacity profile + timeline (draft)

Next steps for Redwood: please send the formal capacity PDF and the runbook so Procurement can attach it to the SOW. Also-- if you can provide a short one-page ops contact list that would be helpful.

Thanks,
Olivia
